New words — 27

Repair — six words that bit you (round two)

xuǎnzé

to choose, pick

Don't lose the n: xuan-zé. You typed it without the n twice.
Wǒ hái méi xuǎnzé hǎo.

I haven't chosen yet.

zhùyì

to watch out; mind (something)

zhùyì = mind/watch out; xiǎoxīn = careful — you typed the wrong sibling.
Zhùyì tīng!

Listen carefully!

guānyú

about, regarding (a topic)

The yù is 4th tone. wèile = 'in order to' — different animal.
Guānyú gōngzuò, wǒmen zài liáo.

About work — let's talk later.

jiéshù

to end, be over

jiéshù = ends; wánle = finished/done for. Second syllable is shù, not she.
Jùhuì jiǔ diǎn jiéshù.

The party ends at nine.

qíshí

actually, to be honest

qí (2nd) shí (2nd). Your mouth wants quì — it's qí, both syllables rise.
Qíshí, wǒ yě bù zhīdào.

Actually, I don't know either.

zhǒng

kind, sort (measure word)

zhǒng = kind/sort; zhāng = flat things (paper, tickets). You keep swapping them.
Zhè zhǒng wǒ bú yào.

This kind — I don't want it.

Change and background

biànhuà

lìshǐ

Wǒ xǐhuan xué lìshǐ

huánjìng

environment

leans written/newsy; for "the place" in casual chat people say dìfang. Keep huánjìng for eco talk and reviews.
Zhèlǐ huánjìng hěn hǎo

The environment here is nice.

gēnjù

semi-formal; in chat people more often say wǒ kàn… "the way I see it" or tā shuō "he said". Understand it, don't lead with it.
Gēnjù tā shuō…

According to him…

jiù

old, worn (things)

exactly the same sound as jiù "then/only" (Day 6 glue) — context only.
Zhè jiàn yīfu tài jiù le

Glue — grammar

A-not-A and tags

Template: Verb-bù-Verb? (chī bu chī? hǎo bu hǎo? shì bu shì?) or statement + hǎo ma? / duì ba?

friendly yes/no questions and "okay?/right?" checks

Nǐ hē bu hē kāfēi?

Do you drink coffee?

Zhège guì bu guì?

Is this expensive?

Wǒmen zǒu ba, hǎo ma?

Let's go — okay?

Foreigner traps

  • Answering with shì — A-not-A wants the verb back: hē! / bù hē, never shì.
  • Two-syllable verbs shorten the FIRST syllable only: chī bu chīfàn is right; chīfàn bu chīfàn is wrong.
  • Don't move the frame to the end: Nǐ xǐhuan zhège bu? is heard but weak — keep verb-bù-verb up front.

A-not-A questions — full guide — Full treatment incl. the two-syllable shortening table and mistake pairs.

zài / zhèngzài + Verb (…ne)

Template: Subject + zhèngzài + Verb + (ne)

"am/is doing right now"; optional ne softens

Wǒ zài chī fàn ne.

I'm eating (right now).

Tāmen zhèngzài kāi huì.

They're in a meeting right now.

Foreigner traps

  • Calquing English 'I am + verb' with shì — shì joins nouns only; shì + verb is never progressive.
  • Habits ≠ zài: 'I'm learning Chinese' as an ongoing project is Wǒ xué Zhōngwén; Wǒ zài xué means right this moment.
  • zài alone before a noun means 'at' (zài jiā = at home) — without a verb after it, you're stating location, not progress.

Native notes — asking questions the way locals do

The short form rule natives actually follow

With two-syllable verbs, A-not-A shortens the FIRST element only: xǐhuan bu xǐhuan can compress to xǐ bu xǐhuan in fast speech — but never xǐhuan bu xǐ. Your ear should expect the clipped version; your mouth can take its time.

A-not-A questions — full guide — Full treatment incl. the two-syllable shortening table and mistake pairs.

hǎo ma? vs hǎo bu hǎo? vs xíng ma? — temperature

hǎo bu hǎo is warm and collaborative (we're deciding together). hǎo ma? is a soft check after you've already decided — asking permission more than opinion. xíng ma? is the practical one — 'does this work for you?' — what you'll hear when someone proposes a plan and wants a green light.

Tag questions — hǎo ma? family — The only page found that actually teaches the temperature differences.

The progressive you'll actually hear

In real conversation zhèngzài often drops to just the verb + ne: Nǐ gànma ne? already means 'what are you doing right now' — no zài needed. The ne is doing the 'right now' work. Hearing this saves you from waiting for a zài that never comes.

Cultural: zǒu bu zǒu?

The old Beijing street-taxi call Zǒu bu zǒu? ('going or not?') survives at stations and tourist spots even in the app era. If a driver asks you this, it means an un-metered ride — the polite defusal is Bú yòng le, xièxie and keep walking toward the official stand.
